status: TASTE SAMPLES — seven founder-ruled families plus one proposed Market/Exchange family; not final table corpus and not live runtime data
sampleLaw: A family chassis may contain only relationships every listed program can honestly consume.
The program layer owns occupation, service, operator, safety, and program-specific obligations.
Operating state and current scene alter a valid program without replacing it.
Spice intensifies a named program surface and preserves program identity.
Realm changes technology, material, labor, practice, etiquette, and spatial emphasis rather than merely relabeling the result.
Prison/Custody is a dedicated family governed by the Site 6 lifecycle.
Market/Exchange remains a proposed eighth family; its sampler output is evidence for founder disposition, not a ruling.

families.label: Public Service / Hospitality
families.sharedGrammar: A legible public arrival meets recognition or payment, an occupied customer area, a service edge, controlled support space, and truthful egress.
forbids: No chassis row decides that the place serves drink, bathing, or gambling.
No private or back-of-house route becomes public merely to solve a scene.

chassis.text: Broad street room with a long service edge; preparation and secure storage sit behind it, with a separate delivery door.
Covered arcade opens into a customer courtyard; two reservable side rooms share a screened service range and rear staff passage.
Corner frontage feeds two connected public rooms around a central recognition desk; service rooms and a narrow staff stair occupy the inner corner.
Long hall divided into a lively front bay and quieter rear bay; payment sits between them, while support runs along one side wall.
Split-level venue with the main public floor above a lower service range; an overlook and separate staff stair keep both levels legible.
Public pavilion inside a larger host building; it owns a staffed service enclosure and secure store but receives one utility from a named shared provider.

states.text: Ordinary service: staffing, supplies, and customer capacity are balanced.
Rush or backlog: the customer floor is full and one service station has become the bottleneck.
Partial operation: one room is closed for repair, cleaning, shortage, or a failed utility.
Reserved use: a private booking or protected clientele controls part of the public floor without erasing ordinary egress.

arrangements.text: Drinkhouse with a public bar, small cold store or cellar, simple food preparation, and no lodging.
Mealhouse with visible kitchen pass, communal tables, a smaller drinking edge, and timed sittings.
Road inn with common room below, guest rooms above or around a court, stable or transport provider, and night access rules.
Member-backed hostelry whose public room remains open while one reservable room and a credit ledger serve regulars.

scenes.text: A delayed drink delivery has the keeper deciding which regulars still receive their usual order.
Two travelers need the last bed, and each claims a different local promise gives them priority.
A meal is leaving the kitchen while its intended table quietly abandons the room.
A tab is being settled with information, but the named person has just entered through the other door.

spice.text: The house ledger shows one patron has been paying another patron's tab for months.
One table is always kept laid for a party whose reservation predates the current keeper.
A drink poured from one marked tap tastes like the last place the customer truly considered home.
Every unpaid promise spoken over the bar becomes audible to its creditor at closing time.

frontier.label: Inn / Alehouse
frontier.realization: Hearth, casks, cellar or cool store, kitchen smoke, stable or road supply, host-led etiquette.

chrome.label: Noodle Bar / Listening House
chrome.realization: Ventilated cookline, refrigeration, compact counter service, booked booths, delivery access, powered light and sound.

gloom.label: Diner / Roadhouse
gloom.realization: Grill line, coffee and bottle storage, booths and counter, back lot delivery, jukebox or radio custom, late-shift staffing.

arrangements.text: Sequential bath with changing, wash room, hot room, cooling edge, and a staffed linen point.
Communal washhouse with timed bathing, laundry service, heated water store, and family/private screens.
Steam house with one shared hot chamber, cold rinse, rest room, and tightly controlled fuel and ventilation.
Appointment bath with several small rooms supplied from one service spine and a shared recovery lounge.

scenes.text: The hot-water queue is slipping, and the keeper must choose between a promised group and ordinary customers.
A missing garment has halted one changing area while attendants compare tags and baskets.
A patron refuses to leave the cooling room until someone hears a private accusation.
A drain inspection has exposed a concealed bundle that clearly entered from inside the bathing circuit.

spice.text: The linen tally proves someone has been using the closed room after hours.
One basin remains warm after the furnace is banked, but only while the room is occupied.
Steam briefly reveals old scars that the bather no longer carries.
Water released from the final drain carries one spoken secret into every connected basin.

frontier.label: Bathhouse / Washhouse
frontier.realization: Boiler or furnace, cisterns, tubs and hot rooms, linen labor, fuel delivery, yard drainage.

chrome.label: Spa / Capsule Bath
chrome.realization: Pumped water, heat exchangers, lockers, filtered wet zones, booking system, maintenance corridors.

gloom.label: Public Baths / Sauna
gloom.realization: Boiler room, tiled wet rooms, lockers and towels, practical ventilation, posted hours, municipal or private keeper.

arrangements.text: Open low-stakes hall with several visible tables, a central cash box, and one floor watcher.
Public front room feeds screened high-stakes tables whose entry and settlement are separately controlled.
Betting house with posted events or contests, ticket/tally counter, result board, and payout window.
Club game room where membership, credit, food and drink service, and private arbitration carry more weight than cash at the table.

scenes.text: A disputed final hand has frozen one table while the house checks the deck and the debt book.
A regular wants their credit extended before a backer arrives to revoke it.
The result board contradicts the sealed tally held behind the counter.
A winner cannot collect because the person authorized to open the reserve has vanished through the staff route.

spice.text: One dealer has been rounding every disputed stake in favor of the same quiet patron.
A retired game table still records wagers in its scarred surface when coins touch it.
One set of dice lands honestly but whispers the result a heartbeat before it stops.
A debt accepted at the private table transfers the debtor's luck to the house until repayment.

frontier.label: Gaming House
frontier.realization: Dice, cards or boards, strongbox, handwritten credit, visible house watcher, food/drink from owned or named provider.

chrome.label: Betting Lounge / Game Club
chrome.realization: Electronic or projected odds, identity-controlled accounts, surveillance, cashier cage, private rooms and service access.

gloom.label: Card Room / Betting Parlor
gloom.realization: Tables and booths, chalk or lit result board, cash window, back-office book, floor manager and parking/alley access.

families.label: Civic / Authority
families.sharedGrammar: A public, member, or duty threshold reaches recognized authority, decision or assembly space, records, a controlled inner zone, and staff circulation.
forbids: No family row supplies involuntary custody as its primary program.
Secure rooms remain subordinate to the selected civic program.

chassis.text: Public counter and waiting bay lead to one decision chamber; records and staff work occupy a controlled rear strip.
Member or petitioner hall faces a raised authority position; two side rooms support consultation, records, or duty work.
Gated court or muster yard leads to a duty room, secure issue store, and command office with a separate staff entrance.
Arcaded public hall separates clerk or recognition desk, formal chamber, private consultation, and a fire-secure record room.
A configurable central floor supports assembly or drill; perimeter offices, issue rooms, and records open from a controlled circulation ring.
Two-storey civic house places public business below and committee, command, or deliberation above; staff and records use a rear stair.

states.text: Ordinary session: public business and staff work follow the posted order.
Handoff: one duty group is replacing another and authority, keys, records, or pending cases are being acknowledged.
Overload: petitioners, members, cases, patrol needs, or records exceed the normal public capacity.
Emergency authority: the public floor remains legible, but one controlled room has become a temporary command or deliberation center.

arrangements.text: Trade guild with dues desk, contract hall, sample or standard display, officers' room, and archive.
Craft guild with member hall, examination bench, shared tools or patterns, stores, and masters' chamber.
Carriers' or labor hall with hiring board, muster floor, relief fund desk, meeting room, and equipment issue.
Merchant association with public arbitration hours, members' exchange floor, private committees, and bonded records.

scenes.text: A candidate's examination piece passes every visible standard but bears a prohibited maker's mark.
Two officers claim authority to sign the same contract before the next caravan departs.
The hiring board lists a crew that insists it never accepted the job.
A relief payment is due, but the member's status was changed during the night.

spice.text: The dues ledger contains a perfectly regular payment from a member everyone remembers burying.
One old standard rejects work made with a technique the current masters cannot identify.
The hall's master pattern subtly alters itself after every unanimous vote.
Any contract sealed in the officers' room compels the guild's building—not its members—to enforce one clause.

frontier.label: Guildhall / Company Hall
frontier.realization: Member marks, samples, contract tables, muster space, physical ledgers, shared stores and officer keys.

chrome.label: Trade Consortium / Labor Exchange
chrome.realization: Credential gates, fabrication standards, data archive, booking floor, committee suites and controlled equipment issue.

gloom.label: Union Hall / Business Association
gloom.realization: Meeting floor, hiring board, records office, sample cases, benefit desk, committee rooms and practical back entrance.

arrangements.text: Town watch station with report desk, muster room, equipment issue, captain's office, and short-rest bunks.
Gate garrison with gate control, guardroom, armory, relief room, wall or road access, and alarm station.
Barracks company with parade or drill court, squad rooms, mess provider, stores, command, and sentry circuit.
Rapid-response post with ready room, vehicle or mount edge, equipment racks, briefing wall, and maintenance supply.

scenes.text: An outgoing patrol refuses to surrender one issued weapon because its replacement crew is incomplete.
A public report contradicts the watch log and the named patrol has not returned to answer it.
The alarm test has revealed that one post receives the signal too late.
A relief crew arrives early carrying orders signed by an authority the commander cannot verify.

spice.text: The equipment ledger shows one shield or protective rig has been issued continuously for years without return.
One alarm station signals a threat category omitted from every current drill.
The muster marks briefly include any absent guard who is in immediate danger.
Weapons drawn from one rack cannot be turned against the authority named at the last shift handoff.

frontier.label: Watch House / Barracks
frontier.realization: Muster yard, arms chest or armory, patrol board, bunks, stable or road access, bells and relief watch.

chrome.label: Security Precinct / Response Hub
chrome.realization: Dispatch wall, controlled equipment lockers, ready bays, surveillance feeds, decontamination or maintenance support.

gloom.label: Sheriff's Office / Armory
gloom.realization: Report counter, squad room, evidence handoff to external custody, gun or gear cage, motor pool or back lot, radio dispatch.

arrangements.text: Single-magistrate court with clerk desk, waiting, hearing room, consultation room, secure records, and bailiff station.
Arbitration hall with several small hearing rooms, shared filing desk, mediators' workroom, and public settlement board.
Circuit court occupying a configurable hall on hearing days and returning records to a traveling or external archive.
Claims and notary court with public counter, document examination, short hearings, payment, and registered issue/appeal route.

scenes.text: Two filed copies of the same order differ by one name, and both bear valid marks.
A hearing cannot begin because the person responsible for interpreting one party's testimony has withdrawn.
A settlement has been reached in private, but the public record would expose a different dispute.
The bailiff has received enforcement instructions before the adjudicator announces a decision.

spice.text: The appeals register shows one case was reopened under a deadline that does not exist in current rules.
A sealed deliberation room carries sound outward only when the speakers agree.
One witness chair grows noticeably heavier with each statement the speaker believes false.
A formally entered judgment changes one physical threshold in the building until appealed or fulfilled.

frontier.label: Magistrate's Court / Hall of Law
frontier.realization: Clerk and petition desk, hearing chamber, seals and ledgers, bailiff route, public notice, nearby external holding if required.

chrome.label: Arbitration Floor / Tribunal
chrome.realization: Identity check, recorded hearing rooms, evidence display, secure files, private deliberation, service and enforcement handoff.

gloom.label: County Court / Municipal Hearing Office
gloom.realization: Clerk counter, courtroom or hearing room, records vault, judge or examiner chamber, sheriff adjacency without prison ownership.

families.label: Household / Estate
families.sharedGrammar: Controlled reception mediates between outside claims and private household life while service circulation, property records, food, sleep, sanitation, dependants, and labor remain credible.
forbids: The Manor cannot be replaced by a shop, hospital, school, or unrelated institution.
A mixed or former use must be selected explicitly and cannot erase the functioning household.

chassis.text: Compact urban manor with formal front rooms, private upper household, rear service court, and separate staff stair.
Courtyard estate with reception and administration on the public side, family rooms on one wing, and kitchens, stores, and staff lodging on another.
Long hall-house with a formal central room, screened service end, private solar or suite, guest chambers, and working yard.
Tower or vertical house with reception below, household rooms above, secure records between them, and service access from a lower side entry.
Estate lodge facing a managed yard or garden; the main house contains reception and family rooms while detached service buildings supply food, storage, and labor.
Divided household around one formal stair: two private branches share reception, kitchen/service, chapel or quiet room, and estate records but control separate thresholds.

states.text: Receiving day: household officers and front rooms are active while private rooms remain controlled.
Private household: ordinary domestic and estate work continues with formal rooms mostly closed.
Understaffed or absent owner: a steward, caretaker, or elder combines several roles and some service spaces are dormant.
Succession or occupation: two claims divide permissions, records, rooms, or staff without changing the building's household identity.

arrangements.text: Resident household led by an owner or elder, with a steward handling petitions, accounts, guests, and estate work.
Absentee owner's house where a bailiff and small permanent household maintain property, rents, repairs, and formal reception.
Multigenerational household whose two branches share service and authority rooms but keep separate private thresholds and dependants.
Official residence where household life coexists with scheduled petitions, audiences, or local administration in the front range.

scenes.text: Two tenants dispute a boundary while the steward discovers that the filed rent roll uses an older property line.
A guest has arrived under a genuine invitation issued by a household member who denies sending it.
The kitchen and stable or transport staff have both been promised the same limited delivery.
A dependant is moving rooms, and every household branch interprets the reassignment as a statement of succession.

spice.text: Two household account books disagree about the support owed to one dependant.
A reception room appears in household inventories but not in the filed plan, although servants describe cleaning it.
Ancestral portraits answer only questions whose subjects were once discussed within their hearing.
One private threshold recognizes a disputed heir as owner and denies the current household head.

frontier.label: Manor / Estate House
frontier.realization: Stewarded reception, household rooms, kitchen and stores, service court, rent or land records, gardens, stable or work providers.

chrome.label: Penthouse / Family Compound
chrome.realization: Controlled lobby, formal entertaining floor, private suites, service elevator or corridor, household staff, asset records and building systems.

gloom.label: Old Family Place / Big House
gloom.realization: Front parlor and dining room, family bedrooms, kitchen and utility rooms, back stair or porch, property office, yard and local dependants.

families.label: Ritual / Institution
families.sharedGrammar: A participant threshold establishes conduct and preparation before a ritual focus, while officiant support, offerings or records, restricted space, services, and gathering remain causally connected.
forbids: A shrine prop cannot substitute for active ritual practice and responsible custody.
Realm symbolism cannot erase participant, officiant, offering, service, or restricted-space relationships.

chassis.text: Axial threshold and preparation bay lead to a common ritual hall and focused sanctuary; officiant rooms and offering store sit behind the focus.
Open court holds gathering and procession; a roofed ritual chamber, side instruction room, and service range form its protected edge.
Congregational hall faces a raised or enclosed focus, with side aisles or paths to private counsel, offerings, storage, and officiant circulation.
Clustered shrine house links several small focuses through one shared preparation room, keeper station, offering record, and quiet court.
A spring, cave, tree, ruin, or other world-owned focus is approached through a managed threshold; shelter, offerings, instruction, and sanitation remain built around it.
Upper public hall and lower restricted chamber share one ritual axis; separate officiant circulation and a service stair preserve access truth.

states.text: Ordinary observance: the focus, officiant support, and public threshold operate on their normal cadence.
Preparation: staff and participants are arranging a rite, teaching, offering, or procession not yet begun.
Festival or crisis attendance: gathering exceeds ordinary interior capacity and uses the approach or court.
Mourning, interdiction, or repair: the main focus is restricted while a smaller valid practice continues elsewhere in the site.

arrangements.text: Congregational temple with scheduled common observance, teaching or counsel, offerings, and an officiant household or staff.
Pilgrimage temple whose approach, reception, offering custody, rest, and crowd cadence matter as much as the inner focus.
Healing or intercession temple with waiting, examination or counsel, ritual treatment, recovery, records, and sanitation.
Keeper shrine serving several household, ancestor, civic, or road observances through a shared threshold and small support range.

scenes.text: An offering has been correctly received but attributed to the wrong petitioner in the public record.
The officiant must decide whether an arriving group may join a rite whose preparation rules they could not have followed.
A healing petitioner asks that the result be recorded under someone else's name.
A maintenance worker has found a message inside a ritual fixture that is not supposed to open.

spice.text: The offering record shows one donor has quietly supported two publicly opposed observances.
One threshold retains the scent, dust, or condensation of the last procession long after cleaning.
The ritual focus answers one repeated gesture differently when performed by someone under an unspoken obligation.
An accepted offering transfers its attached vow to the next person who removes it without authority.

frontier.label: Temple / Shrine House
frontier.realization: Processional or public threshold, altar or world focus, offerings, lamps and fuel, keeper rooms, instruction, charity or healing provider.

chrome.label: Sanctum / Reflection Clinic
chrome.realization: Controlled quiet threshold, immersive or technical focus, scheduled sessions, secure offerings/data, counselors or officiants, life-safety systems.

gloom.label: Church / Roadside Chapel / Healing Mission
gloom.realization: Vestibule, sanctuary or meeting hall, office and counsel room, donation records, kitchen or aid provider, practical maintenance and community schedule.

families.label: Logistics
families.sharedGrammar: A receiving edge converts arriving goods into identified, handled, stored, counted, and dispatched loads through staff-controlled routes connected to real vehicles or carriers.
forbids: Storage cannot be an inert pile without ownership, route, handling, and dispatch truth.
A dock relationship requires actual water, vehicle, loading, or transfer facts.

chassis.text: Street receiving doors open to inspection and sorting; storage bays fill the rear while a separate dispatch lane reaches the opposite side.
Vehicle yard fronts covered loading sheds and deep storage; counting office and secure goods room overlook the shared handling court.
Tall store uses a hoist or lift beside stacked floors; receiving, weighing, and dispatch remain separated at ground level.
A long transit shed has numbered temporary bays, cross-aisles, a tally station, and direct loading edges on both long sides.
Secure compact store combines intake, weighing, and dispatch at one controlled desk while dangerous or valuable goods occupy separated cells.
Waterside or vehicle-side house bridges a public paperwork front to a restricted loading platform, with manifests, gear, short-term storage, and staff rest behind.

states.text: Normal throughput: arriving, stored, and departing loads fit the handling and record capacity.
Arrival surge: one carrier has delivered early and sorting or temporary storage is consuming a route.
Inventory discrepancy: physical goods, seals, ownership, or manifest totals do not reconcile.
Hazard or access loss: weather, damage, contamination, labor dispute, tide, or vehicle failure has closed one handling edge.

arrangements.text: Merchant warehouse with long-term owned bays, sample or inspection bench, counting office, and scheduled customer dispatch.
Bonded store where seals, customs or authority, secure cages, and release orders control movement.
Transit warehouse with numbered short-stay bays, cross-docking, rapid tally, and little long-term storage.
Special-condition store whose cool, dry, ventilated, guarded, or hazardous bays create distinct handling and failure rules.

scenes.text: A sealed load occupies the correct bay but the seal belongs to a different owner.
Workers refuse to move one crate because its recorded weight changes between stations.
A customer arrives with a valid release order for goods already staged for someone else.
A roof or utility failure is forcing a rapid choice about which goods receive the remaining protected space.

spice.text: One numbered bay has been paid for continuously although no employee remembers seeing it occupied.
Dust settles everywhere except along a handling route absent from the current floor plan.
Goods placed in one bay acquire the smell and temperature of their intended destination.
Any load left after its release date begins replacing nearby labels with its own destination.

frontier.label: Warehouse / Storehouse
frontier.realization: Cart court, loading doors, hoist, timber racks, seals and ledgers, watchman, roof and damp control.

chrome.label: Freight Depot / Secure Storage
chrome.realization: Loading bays, lifts, tracked units, climate or hazard zones, scanners, dispatch office and controlled vehicle circulation.

gloom.label: Warehouse / Distribution Shed
gloom.realization: Truck dock or rail siding, pallets and shelves, receiving office, cages, inventory sheets, forklifts or hand gear, roof and utility risk.

arrangements.text: Harbormaster or quay office with public berth desk, tide and arrival board, restricted platform access, signal gear, and incident records.
Stevedore dispatch house with hiring/muster, gear issue, gang assignment, tally, and direct loading-platform route.
Customs or bonded dock-house with declaration counter, inspection, seal store, temporary hold, and release to vessel or road.
Ferry or packet house with ticket/booking, waiting, baggage, crew room, timetable, and controlled gangway or vehicle ramp.

scenes.text: Two vessels or carriers claim the same berth under different valid schedules.
A labor gang has assembled, but its gear was issued to a crew that never appeared.
An arriving passenger's baggage bears a cargo seal and is being diverted to inspection.
The weather or tide board has changed while the instrument or observer responsible still reports the earlier reading.

spice.text: The berth book reserves one arrival every week for a carrier no current worker has seen.
One length of platform remains wet or frost-marked regardless of tide and weather.
The arrival board posts one vessel or vehicle a day before any message announces it.
A cargo accepted under the wrong destination begins pulling its carrier toward that destination when departure starts.

frontier.label: Harbor House / Quay Office
frontier.realization: Tide board, berth book, signal mast, cranes or tackle, gang muster, bonded shed and boat/cart access.

chrome.label: Port Control / Freight Interface
chrome.realization: Traffic display, berth locks, cargo screening, powered lifts, secure holds, crew access, weather and system redundancy.

gloom.label: Dock Office / Ferry Terminal
gloom.realization: Ticket or manifest counter, radio room, waiting, baggage and freight shed, gangway controls, back-lot loading and storm procedure.

families.label: Shop / Workshop
families.sharedGrammar: A customer or commission edge connects to transaction, stock, work or preparation where required, secure material, utilities and waste, operator position, and delivery.
forbids: A family chassis is occupation-neutral; printer, smith, apothecary, or other source occupants never migrate with geometry.
Each program must supply its own work, safety, storage, and professional-service obligations.

chassis.text: Street counter leads to a rear workroom, secure store, and service yard with delivery and waste access.
Open work bay faces a customer edge; materials occupy a side room while office, valuables, and records sit behind the operator.
Domestic front room serves customers beside an attached workshop; a rear delivery passage separates supplies and waste from household access.
Arcade stall owns a lockable counter and demonstration surface while a shared back passage reaches a dedicated store or offsite workshop.
Corner shop combines two display fronts, a screened consultation or fitting alcove, rear work/preparation, and a cool or secure cellar.
Yard-front workshop places noisy, hot, bulky, or hazardous work in a covered bay; office/counter, material shed, and delivery gate stay separately controllable.

states.text: Ordinary trade: work, stock, customer service, utilities, and delivery are balanced.
Demand backlog: customer orders, consultations, preparations, repairs, or commissions exceed the current operator's time or safe capacity.
Supply shortage: one controlled material or external provider is delaying otherwise valid work.
Inspection or repair: one work surface, utility, safety control, or storage zone is unavailable and changes service.

arrangements.text: Repair smith with public commission desk, general forge, quench, parts stock, and an active queue of ordinary tools and fittings.
Production forge with repeated work stations, fuel and bar stock, finishing bench, quality check, and dispatch for contracted batches.
Armorer with fitting space, secure finished stock, heatwork separated from customers, and records for issued or commissioned protection.
Farrier or vehicle smith with yard access, animal or chassis restraint, hoof/wheel fittings, forge, and safe waiting edge.

scenes.text: An expensive commission is complete, but the person named to collect it denies ordering it.
A cracked tool from a local crew reveals the same flaw in several pieces from one material batch.
The quench or cooling system has been reserved for urgent work that has not yet arrived.
A customer demands a repair while refusing to surrender the damaged object's concealed attachment.

spice.text: An expensive commission remains uncollected while storage fees quietly exceed its final payment.
A sealed chimney or power duct implies an inaccessible former hearth or work bay.
Tools return to their assigned places and continue the last motion taught by a dead master.
Metal worked here refuses to cross one named threshold while hot.

frontier.label: Smithy / Forge
frontier.realization: Forge and fuel, bellows or draft, anvil and benches, quench, bar/scrap stock, yard delivery, sparks and fire control.

chrome.label: Fabrication Shop / Machine Bay
chrome.realization: Powered tools, welding or thermal work, ventilation, parts racks, inspection, secure commissions and loading bay.

gloom.label: Repair Garage / Metal Shop
gloom.realization: Service counter, work bays, torch or welder, parts cage, fluids and waste, lift or yard, job tickets and practical fire safety.

arrangements.text: Retail dispensary with front counter, screened advice, rear compounding, ordinary stock, controlled cabinet, and delivery record.
Consultation practice with waiting, private examination or counsel, small preparation room, medicine store, wash point, and patient notes.
Domestic herbal practice with customer room, drying and preparation, garden or supplier relation, cool store, and household boundary.
Clinic-apothecary with triage counter, treatment room, dispensary, cold or secure stock, sanitation, and separate clinical waste.

scenes.text: An assistant is preparing a renewal signed before the physician or authorizing practitioner died.
Two remedies with similar labels require opposite storage, and one has been returned to the wrong shelf.
A supplier offers the missing ingredient only if the practitioner accepts an unrecorded substitute batch.
A patient reports a side effect that matches another customer's formula rather than their own.

spice.text: A renewable prescription bears the signature of a practitioner known to be dead.
The cold store remains cold without a visible mechanism, but its temperature log is otherwise ordinary.
Several remedies consistently treat a different mapped condition than the wording on their labels.
One preparation transfers a symptom into the next person who enters the consultation alcove.

frontier.label: Apothecary / Herbalist
frontier.realization: Herbs and compounds, drying or supplier route, scales and preparation, water and heat, cool/secure stock, consultation and waste.

chrome.label: Unlicensed Clinic / Med Shop
chrome.realization: Waiting and diagnostic surface, cold storage, sterile preparation, disposables, locked drugs, ventilation and clinical waste.

gloom.label: Drugstore / Back Clinic
gloom.realization: Prescription counter, shelves and stockroom, back consultation, refrigerator, sink and sanitation, controlled cabinet, delivery and records.

arrangements.text: Counter store with dense shelves, requested goods behind the keeper, back stock, bulk delivery, and household credit book.
Open browse shop with visible ordinary goods, staffed counter, secure valuables, packing bench, and rear receiving.
Supply depot serving travelers or crews through prepacked kits, bulk staples, special orders, and a loading yard.
Village store and post or message counter sharing one public room while parcels, stock, accounts, and private correspondence remain separated.

scenes.text: The last unit of an ordinary necessity has been promised to two customers under different forms of credit.
A special order arrived correctly addressed but contains the standard goods for another climate or region.
A supplier's invoice proves several shelf prices are now below replacement cost.
A returned kit is complete except for one cheap item whose absence makes the rest unsafe to use.

spice.text: The credit book carries a household that no longer exists, yet someone keeps making exact payments.
One shelf is always stocked in the order customers will request its goods that day.
A sealed travel kit contains one modest item appropriate to the buyer's next serious delay.
Goods purchased on credit begin wearing the marks of the lender's household until the debt is settled.

frontier.label: General Store / Provisioner
frontier.realization: Counter and shelves, bulk bins, rope and tools, back stock, delivery yard, handwritten orders and household credit.

chrome.label: Supply Kiosk / Utility Mart
chrome.realization: Modular goods, locked technical stock, pickup counter, inventory system, parcel lockers, loading or courier edge.

gloom.label: Hardware and Grocery / Corner Store
gloom.realization: Aisles and counter, stockroom, cooler or utility goods, loading alley, layaway or account book, local parcel service.

arrangements.text: Component shop with consultation counter, ordinary reagents, locked rare stock, verification bench, and controlled disposal.
Scroll, pattern, or encoded-work dealer with reading desk, copying or activation room, secure archive, and provenance records.
Commission workshop with customer interview, isolated fabrication cell, test surface, material store, and collection protocol.
Appraisal and ward service with intake quarantine, diagnostic bench, consultation, secure hold, and return or escalation route.

scenes.text: A component passes every test but its provenance belongs to a batch recorded as destroyed.
A customer wants an appraisal without allowing the object to cross the shop's intake boundary.
A completed commission responds correctly to the wrong authorized user.
The disposal container is full because one harmless residue refuses to become inert.

spice.text: A rare component's provenance record names a perfectly ordinary supplier who denies ever handling it.
The demonstration surface retains a faint diagram of the last failed test until a successful one replaces it.
One locked drawer opens only when the requester accurately states what they will not use its contents for.
Any unreceipted component leaving the shop causes its storage condition to manifest around the carrier.

frontier.label: Arcanist / Charmwright
frontier.realization: Component drawers, consultation, inscribed or worked bench, locked cabinet, test circle or safe surface, provenance and disposal.

chrome.label: Esoteric Tech / Black Clinic
chrome.realization: Controlled components, diagnostic instruments, isolated work cell, access logs, shielding or ventilation, hazardous waste and secure pickup.

gloom.label: Occult Supply / Repair Office
gloom.realization: Front counter, reference files, back workroom, locked case, test bench, practical containment, alley delivery and discreet appointments.

families.label: Market / Exchange (proposed eighth family)
families.sharedGrammar: A publicly legible trading ground allocates pitches or bays, admits goods and buyers on a schedule, exposes inspection and common measure, records price or obligation, supports delivery and clearing, and closes without erasing ownership or access truth.
forbids: No civic chamber, warehouse, or row of unrelated shops may replace the trading-ground program merely because it shares the building.
Stalls, samples, standards, and goods are assigned operating surfaces, not undifferentiated market dressing.
An optional upper program must declare its own Civic, Logistics, or Exchange obligations while the ground-floor market remains independently legible.

chassis.text: Open-post market house: a roofed rectangular trading floor is divided by repeated structural bays, with open cross-access, an authority-and-measure position, and loading or clearing at one short end.
Pier-and-arch hall: a heavier open arcade encloses a durable market floor, with perimeter pitch lines, two public approaches, a lockable standards room, and a service edge.
Long exchange hall: a broad central aisle separates parallel trading bays while an inspection rail, clerk position, sample hold, and end loading doors keep bargaining distinct from bulk movement.
Court-and-arcade market: permanent covered bays line one or more sides of an open court, with a common measure point, removable fair pitches, drainage, and several closure gates.

Two-level market house: an open trading ground and lockable count room sit below an external or controlled stair to a separately accountable upper program; delivery and public circulation do not pass through that upper room.

Deep cloth-hall lattice: repeated arcaded or post bays flank a continuous inspection-and-display route, with folding or sample tables, secure standards and records, side delivery courts, and an upper storage or bargaining range.

states.text: Opening and allocation: officials, keepers, or elected traders assign pitches, check rights, set out standards, and separate deliveries from the arriving public.
Full trade: bargaining, inspection, weighing, payment, replenishment, and crowd movement compete for the same legible bays and aisles.
Clearing and closure: portable pitches are struck, unsold goods are attributed and removed or secured, accounts close, refuse leaves, and public routes reopen.
Assay or dispute session: one standard, lot, allocation, price, or right to trade is under public examination while the rest of the market continues around it.

guestCompositions.text: The market ground keeps its own pitches, measure, schedule, delivery, closure, and authority. A separately reached upper council chamber or court consumes Civic/Authority threshold, decision, staff, and records obligations without commandeering the trading floor.

Upper or side storage receives named lots from the market's delivery edge through a controlled goods route. Logistics owns custody, handling, count, and dispatch; the public floor still owns allocation, inspection, price, and market hours.

An upper bargaining, sample, or record hall relates registered contracts and lots to the market below through attributed stairs and goods routes. It extends the family but does not make the public ground optional.

arrangements.text: Daily provisions market with assigned food and household-goods bays, a common scale, early delivery, public trading hours, wash-down, and same-day clearing.
Periodic town market whose permanent hall stores standards and allocation records while removable pitches and carts expand onto an adjoining court on market day.
Mixed market with several licensed permanent counters at the sheltered edge and numbered temporary pitches on the central floor, all sharing inspection and closure rules.
Wholesale-first hall where bulk lots are inspected and priced before dawn, then broken into smaller public sales while separate delivery and buyer routes remain active.

scenes.text: Two traders hold valid-looking allocations for the same numbered pitch, and opening cannot finish until the authority record is reconciled.
The common scale is accurate, but a legal local weight now differs from the standard stamped into several prepaid deliveries.
A late cart blocks the clearing route while its perishable load is owed to buyers already waiting at three different bays.
An order closes one category of trade at midday, leaving goods, deposits, and promised collection times that still belong to named people.

spice.text: Old pitch marks beneath the current numbering prove one narrow bay was quietly removed from the allocation book.
A suspended balance rings at a distinct pitch whenever a weighed lot contains goods from two declared origins.
At the opening call, each numbered bay casts the shadow of the goods contractually promised there, including one promise no trader admits making.
A licensed market bell shifts one complete, attributed pitch between two approved trading grounds at closure; goods, keeper, records, routes, and claims move together.

frontier.label: Market House / Covered Market
frontier.realization: Timber posts or stone arcades shelter numbered pitches, common beam and stamped weights, clerk or reeve, cart edge, wash-down and a bell-governed market day.

chrome.label: Wholesale Concourse / Regulated Market
chrome.realization: Modular vendor bays, booking and identity gates, calibrated inspection stations, live price boards, cold or secure services, freight edge and timed public access.

gloom.label: Municipal Market Shed / Produce Hall
gloom.realization: Painted stall numbers, concrete or iron bays, scale office, cash and account counter, loading alley, drains and refuse route, shutters and posted market hours.

arrangements.text: Cloth hall with long merchant bays, daylight inspection, measuring and folding tables, stamped quality records, secure samples, and bulk bales entering from side courts.
Commodity exchange where samples and lot records reach a bargaining floor while the physical bulk remains in attributed stores connected to a timed delivery edge.
Merchants' exchange with posted prices, agent benches, private bargaining recesses, contract registration, settlement, and an arbitration room reached without crossing secure records.
Seasonal fair hall whose permanent standards, clerk, sample store, and dispute process support a changing licensed commodity and temporary merchant roster.

scenes.text: A sealed sample passes inspection, but the attributed bulk lot arriving at the side court carries a different handling mark.
Two recognized standards produce different grades for the same cloth, and both authorities have buyers waiting on the result.
The posted price changed during a delayed message interval, leaving matched contracts that are legal under different recorded minutes.
A registered merchant has vanished after assigning both a sample and a delivery obligation to different agents with valid seals.

spice.text: A retired assay stamp appears on one current lot record and on no physical bale yet admitted to the hall.
The north inspection light reveals repairs and substitutions that disappear under every lamp used elsewhere in the hall.
A retained sample changes scent and temperature to match the present storage condition of its attributed bulk lot.
When a contract is publicly settled, its attributed lot acquires the hall's mark wherever it physically rests; forged settlement can therefore move both title and danger.

frontier.label: Cloth Hall / Wool Exchange
frontier.realization: Long arcaded hall, cloth or sample bays, daylight tables, beam and measures, guild or town clerk, sealed records, bale court and upper store or bargaining room.

chrome.label: Commodity Exchange / Clearing Hall
chrome.realization: Credentialed trading floor, certified sample lab, market data and bid surfaces, contract clearing, bonded custody, freight-system links and controlled records.

gloom.label: Produce Exchange / Merchants' Hall
gloom.realization: Inspection tables under high windows, chalk price board or ticker, agent rail, sample cages, stamped tickets, warehouse and rail or truck transfer, arbitration office.

families.label: Prison / Custody
families.sharedGrammar: An authority receives identifiable people and property, classifies and assigns them to controlled holding, sustains service and routine, applies a disposition, and exposes precommitted routes to release, transfer, escape, rescue, force, failure, and aftermath.
forbids: No civic room list, cellblock label, or security skin substitutes for the eight custody circuits.
No generated prison may require narrator mercy or one impossible check as its only exit.
Prisoner property, case evidence, contraband, and institution property retain distinct identities even when they share a secure realization.

chassis.text: Rung-A watchhouse: public keeper threshold, one controlled holding room or cell, staff-side property cabinet, external service route, and explicit release or transfer.
Keeper-house civic jail: street-facing keeper room, controlled inner threshold, short cell bank, raised landing, walled yard, intake-side property closet, and rear household/service access.
Ledger-and-shift jail: waiting and intake-search, staff-only attributed property, numbered holding children, count/handoff station, control landing, yard, and separate staff/service route.
Bounded-liberty court: controlled outer gate surrounds rooms or wards, supervised common movement, visitor/account edge, services, and a strong release/re-arrest boundary.
Gallery wing: reception and classification feed repeated cells along an observed gallery, with staff spine, service hatches, yard or work route, property store, and emergency release.

Warded exceptional holding: one or more cells depend on a visible support, energy, name, living material, gravity, or suspension system with operator access, service rig, property destination, emergency release, and honest failure surfaces.

states.text: Routine custody: count, meals or service, visits or hearings, staff relief, and disposition proceed on their committed cadence.
Admission or transfer surge: intake, search, classification, property, and assignment are under visible load.
Overcapacity or restricted movement: classification and services are strained, but the compiler retains truthful routes and consequences.
Partial containment failure: one force, permission, service, or control layer is damaged or desynchronized and alert has changed access.

arrangements.text: Keeper-House Civic Custody: authority and several circuits concentrate in a named keeper and attached household while cells, property, yard, and service remain explicit.
Ledger-and-Shift Civic Custody: numbered people and holdings, signed commitment/release, attributed property, count/handoff, and role-bound access survive staff change.
Short-Hold Watchhouse: one operator combines intake, oversight, record, and release while a single holding, property cabinet, and external services preserve the complete lifecycle.
Warded Exceptional Custody: a licensed world mechanism replaces some ordinary barriers but retains operator, support, service, property, disposition, emergency release, and all plan families.

scenes.text: The count is correct, but one held person is assigned to the wrong stable holding child and the reason matters before the next movement.
A valid release or transfer order has arrived while the attributed property container cannot be reconciled with its receipt.
A meal, water, waste, medical, repair, or operator-relief provider has missed its cadence, opening one route while worsening another condition.
The disposition clock advances at the next handoff, but the authority record, keeper testimony, and prisoner's identity do not agree.

spice.text: One cell can be opened from inside because of a known maintenance fault scheduled for repair after the next transfer.
A custody room exists in current records but is absent from the public plan; staff route references prove it is not invented on discovery.
One lock recognizes legal disposition rather than its physical key, creating both a lawful route and a falsification target.
At shift change one holding changes physical destination while preserving its occupants, support demands, property links, and failure surfaces.

frontier.label: Gaol / Stockade / Keeper-House Jail
frontier.realization: Commission or court claim, keeper or shift, cells/pen/yard, keys and records, property cabinet/store, household or civic services, road transfer and finite disposition.

chrome.label: Detention / Processing Unit
chrome.realization: Identity and intake search, controlled property, modular or specialized holdings, access systems, surveillance, service and medical routes, shift handoff, emergency release.

gloom.label: County Jail / Lockup
gloom.realization: Booking desk, holding cells or short block, property bags and evidence handoff, control booth or keeper station, meal and medical provider, court/road transfer and release desk.
